SnapWheel Snapshot Wheel v1.2.0
========================================

Author: exper7
Portable and installation-free: Double-click SnapWheel.exe to use it without installing anything (Windows 7 / 10 / 11).
On Windows 7, the "Text Capture" feature requires an additional local component included with the package; see the Win7 package on the Release page. (Windows 10 / 11 can use the system's built-in version.)


[First Launch]
  A beginner guide will automatically pop up once; just read it and close it.
  ★ The guide window **can be resized by dragging its border**; the text will rewrap accordingly — if you cannot see all content on a small laptop screen, simply drag it larger.
  Afterwards, it will hide in the system tray at the bottom-right corner, with a small wheel icon attached to the screen corner.


[Basic Usage]
  Screenshot    Ctrl+Shift+S → Drag to select an area, resize by dragging corners, rotate by dragging the rotation knob on top,
                confirm with double-click or Enter; press Right Click while selecting to cancel (it will not pop up on the desktop).
  Annotate      After taking a screenshot, do not rush to confirm: the toolbar above the floating layer has Arrow / Box / Mosaic / Text
                (shortcuts A / R / M / T), available in four colors. Ctrl+Z to undo, Ctrl+Y to redo.
                After typing text, you can drag its position and change size with the scroll wheel; press B to toggle off the white background if desired.
  Stick to Screen The **nail at the far right of the floating layer toolbar**: after selecting an area, click it to instantly pin the image at your selected location,
                while it is also saved normally to the wheel. You can also use the mouse middle button on thumbnails:
                scroll to zoom, drag to move, double-click or press Esc to close; the tray offers a one-click option to remove all pinned images.
  Text Capture (OCR) Click "Text" on the toolbar (or press O) → Drag a box around the text → It will be recognized and automatically copied.
                In the result window, you can also translate the result to Chinese / English with one click.
                If you don't want to take a screenshot: Right-click the tray → "Text Capture: Recognize image in clipboard".
                In the result window, there is a line for "OCR Engine"; you can choose: Automatic (recommended) / System Built-in (fast, but short titles and small text may cause entire lines to be missed) / Included Local Component (slower, full screen takes 3~4 seconds, fewer missed characters). After selection, the same image will be recognized again.
  Long Screenshot Click "Long Image" on the floating layer toolbar, then slowly scroll down the page yourself; it will stitch each screen into one long image.
                ★ **Only the content that scrolls with your box is selected** — sidebar, browser tabs, and floating windows
                  which **do not scroll** will be treated as new content and stitched in screen by screen.
                  This is the boundary of this long screenshot method; similar tools behave the same way.
                ★ The taskbar strip has been automatically excluded; no need to avoid it yourself.
  Pass Mode     Ctrl+Alt+C — Send images without using the mouse:
                First, use the scroll wheel to select the image you want to send, press the hotkey to enter Pass Mode, a "fake cursor" appears on screen,
                and the selected thumbnail sticks to the bottom-right corner. Switch to WeChat / documents yourself via Alt+Tab,
                move the fake cursor using **arrow keys** (Shift for acceleration), and press Space to place it.
                [ ] Switch image, C to copy without pasting, Esc to cancel.
                ★ Recommended to use arrow keys: WASD also works, but will type letters into the target window.
  Save As       Press Ctrl+S on a thumbnail (select path and format); click a grid once to copy it itself
                (image = image; text grid = that segment of text; file grid = that file); double-click to open.
  Undo Delete   Don't panic if you delete by mistake: Right-click the tray → "Undo Last Deletion",
                the batch just deleted (the whole batch if cleared at once) will be returned to the original disk, and up to the last 8 deletions are remembered.
                (Only deletions during this session are remembered; exiting the program clears them — please drag images you want to keep long-term into a folder for safekeeping.)
  Flip Image    Hover mouse over the wheel and scroll

View Large Image      Hold on a thumbnail for about 0.3 seconds to enlarge the preview (zoom level adjustable)
  Drag Out         Drag a tile to WeChat / folder / anywhere (dragging a text tile to the desktop creates a .txt file)
                    ★ Default: "Keep a copy after dragging out" — the item does not disappear from the ring (dragging itself is a copy operation)
  Drag Back         Drag from desktop / browser / anywhere into here: images become image tiles, other files (PDF, zip, documents)
                    become "file tiles"; selecting and dragging **a segment of text** from a webpage or Notepad = "text tile".
                    Tile appearance follows content: images = glass cards, text / files = a piece of paper.
                    File tiles are color-coded by type for instant recognition: document=blue, spreadsheet=green, presentation=orange, archive=yellow,
                    media=purple, program=gray; unrecognized items retain the natural paper color.
  Move In           Settings on page 1 (bottom) can enable "Move In" for files dragged in: files are **moved** from their original location (not copied),
                    recoverable from Recycle Bin; if unchecked, originals remain (default, and prompts will tell you where to open them after dragging in).
                    ★ When Recycle Bin is unavailable (network drives, read-only locations), it **never deletes the original**, leaves a copy in the ring, and informs you directly.
                    ★ "Move In" only moves from the original location when activated; if files are already in place (move failed or switch unchecked),
                      deleting a tile simply removes that tile from the ring, **it does not affect files on your drive**.
  Copy to Ring      "Copy" an image anywhere, and it automatically slides into the wheel (can be disabled in settings)
  Change Wheel      Long-press the inner disk on the ring (universal key): Up=New, Right=Next, Down=Delete, Left=Previous;
                    Release while on "Delete" turns left half green=Cancel / right half red=Confirm
  Rename            Hover mouse over a name pill on the wheel, click once to rename, and select "What this ring collects"
                    (Collect all / images only / text only — items not collected are blocked upon drag-in with a notification)
                    ★ Screenshot hotkeys ignore this: pressing the key always produces an image; screenshots won't be lost even if "this ring doesn't collect images"
  Import Images     Right-click tray → Import Images… (multiple selection allowed)
  Show / Hide       Double-click tray, or tray menu "Show/Hide Wheel"


【Supported Image Formats】
  png / jpg / jpeg / bmp / gif / tif / ico / webp / heic / avif / jxl / camera RAW …
  Dragging folders also works (automatically takes files from the first layer, max 50 at once); non-image files become "file tiles".
  Opaque photos are saved as JPEG, transparent ones as PNG; large images over 4096px are automatically resized to 4096.


【Settings Options】
  Behavior         Save to disk, auto-start on boot, save directory, screenshot hotkey, ring corner position, delete method, Wheel switching mode,
                    auto-collapse when idle, always on top, keep copy after dragging out, clipboard auto-collection, "Move In" for dragged-in files
  Appearance       Thumbnail size, ring radius, arc tile count, serial number font size, long-press zoom level, startup animation toggle
  Style            Interface style (Neumorphism+Glass / Pure Flat / High Contrast), theme color, glass opacity,
                    card border radius, shadow intensity, animation speed, name/count label toggles,
                    glass blur refresh timer, ripples, ring shadow, time perception (all can be individually disabled)
  Advanced         Interface scaling, interface style details, translation interface
  ★ "Make wheel visible during screen recording" at bottom of Style page:
    Wheel is invisible to screen capture by default (so it won't appear in your own screenshots),
    but the marker on Windows 10 2004+ **blocks even screen recording** — enable this if you want to record demo videos.
    (This marker doesn't exist on Windows 7: wheel is always visible, so this option has no effect there.)
    After enabling, the wheel will also appear in your screenshots; remember to turn it off after recording.


【Resolution / Scaling】

The entire wheel scales proportionally with the monitor's DPI (text and icons grow together), so it won't distort on 2K, 4K, or small laptop screens; using it across multiple monitors with different scaling settings is also fine.  
To manually adjust: Settings → Advanced → Interface Scaling (Auto / 80% ~ 250%).  
If the content doesn't fit, it will automatically scale down one more level and won't push content off-screen.


【Two common pitfalls, clarified upfront】
1. Do not run as "Run as administrator".  
   Windows will block drag-and-drop between administrator programs and the desktop/Explorer, resulting in "no matter how you drag, it won't enter".  
   If accidentally started as administrator, a bubble notification will appear in the tray; right-clicking the tray offers "Restart with normal privileges".
2. When dragging an image into the wheel, if the wheel is in display state (hidden when no window is shown), it cannot accept the drag.
3. When taking a screenshot, a certain window "disappears" (most typical is WeChat): that is because **that program itself prevents screenshots**  
   (it sets Windows to "Exclude me from screenshots"), and this applies to any similar tool — including Win+Shift+S.  
   It is not SnapWheel malfunctioning.


【Automatic Updates】
Right-click the tray → "Check for updates". If a new version is found, it will download and ask whether you want to restart and install now.  
You can also disable automatic checks at startup in Settings.


【Where Data Is Stored】
Settings        %APPDATA%\SnapWheel\settings.ini  
Wheel List     %APPDATA%\SnapWheel\wheels.ini  
Error Log      %APPDATA%\SnapWheel\error.log (the program does not exit abnormally due to issues; all problems are recorded here)  
Saved Screenshots   The "Save Directory" in Settings, defaulting to Pictures\SnapWheel (must enable "Save to Disk" in Settings)  
Usage Statistics   Disabled by default. When enabled, it only records on the local machine which feature was used and how many images are on each ring; it does not record window titles, file names, or text on images, and **does not upload anything**  
To Restore Defaults   Delete the entire %APPDATA%\SnapWheel folder and restart (equivalent to a fresh install)
